Hi Alex / Priya - quick technical note that should answer most of the benchmarking asks before the deep-dive. I'll bring detailed graphs on Friday, but high-level: 

A) Benchmark assumptions I used for the attached matrix:
- Model family: Llama-3-like architecture (comparable compute/kv-flops) on A100/4090-class instance profiles.
- Output size: 256 tokens unless otherwise noted.
- Stream vs non-stream: streaming measured as first-byte latency (time to first token) and tail measured as time to last token.

B) Context window impact (rules of thumb)
- Small contexts (<=4k tokens): end-to-end p95 dominated by model compute - for typical gen configs p95 ~120-220ms for non-streaming; streaming first-byte ~80-130ms.
- Medium contexts (4k-16k): KV cache growth increases per-token memory/lookup overhead; p95 non-streaming jumps to ~180-400ms depending on batching; streaming first-byte typically increases ~30-80ms vs small contexts because we need to load more KV pages.
- Large contexts (>16k): memory pressure triggers larger kernels / possible spilling - expect p95 to increase nonlinearly; we recommend Dedicated with higher memory GPU profiles or sharded KV to keep p95 predictable.

C) Batching and concurrency tradeoffs
- Continuous batching reduces average cost but increases p95 tail when batch windows grow. For your target concurrency (40-60 sustained, spikes to 150):
  - If you prioritize latency, use smaller batch windows (10-20ms) and autoscale more aggressively - this keeps p95 low but increases cost.
  - If you prioritize cost, accept larger batch windows (40-100ms) and slightly higher p95 during spikes. We can configure dynamic batching based on queue length to balance this.

D) Streaming specifics
- We can emit first tokens before the full context is inspected by doing prefix processing. For very long contexts this adds an upfront cost to build necessary KV ranges, but it is possible to get first-byte latencies comparable to medium contexts with careful kernel selection and partial KV loading.

E) Dedicated GPU recommendations (high-level)
- 16k context: 80-96 GB-class GPU (or multi-GPU sharded) to avoid spilling; tuned kernel set and quantization recommended.
- 32k context: recommend sharded Dedicated (2+ GPU) or a 256GB-hosted profile; otherwise we see tail risk.

Deliverables for Fri's call
- I'll bring a p50/p95 table for streaming/non-streaming across 1k/4k/16k inputs and two operation points (low-latency / cost-optimized).
- I'll include a short recommended config (batch window, batch size cap, autoscale thresholds) for your deployment.

Attaching the redwood-latency-matrix.xlsx we referenced - contains the baseline numbers and test config.
